The user asked to return to PR #25 and address its new comments. The expert
[comment](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/25#issuecomment-5890301780)
asks how the gaps compare with ATLAS/CMS and whether bundle load grows toward
the outermost endcap. Observed review head:
`2a3dbfb741f7ea27e77cca3de81690fa800e4567`. PR remains draft; PR #24's tracker
hypothesis is unapproved. No gap resizing, row recovery, layer optimization,
production integration or new physics acceptance is authorized by this response.

Preserved the four unrelated untracked usage files. Ordinary merge of origin/main
retained the separately completed branch-restoration journal. This is a new
bounded session, with no duplicated usage observations.
events.content_kind: curated_excerpt; retain original qualifiers and speaker labels

events.text: Compare service gaps with upgrade trackers and expose cumulative routing loads — see the canonical narrative for outcomes and checks.

The user explicitly corrected the approval boundary: PR #24 did not approve the
tracker default; use it only as a working hypothesis. They requested TDR-based
support/cable/cooling estimates, actual gaps between pixel/short and short/long
packages, conditional outer long-strip routing, radial barrel exits and mockups.
Layer-position optimization is deferred to a separate follow-up PR.

Start: main at `1aa2aafd381fc37a9da3368686f2ca34d9f4dd0a`, the PR24 merge.
Branch: `study/tracker-service-corridors`. Four pre-existing untracked usage
summary files are preserved and excluded from this task's commits. DES-010 was
drafted before the service overlay. No production geometry, material model,
reconstruction configuration or approval state is changed.
